edges.description: Loss of the NSMCE3-NSMCE4 interface weakens the subcomplex that bridges the SMC5 and SMC6 subunits, so the complex as a whole is destabilized.
The SMC5/6 complex resolves recombination intermediates; its destabilization impairs double-strand break repair by homologous recombination while sparing nonhomologous end joining.
Loss of SMC5/6 function prevents restart of DNA replication after a hydroxyurea block, a defect shared with NSMCE2-deficient cells.

Lung injury that develops without preceding infection and with normal immune studies suggests a route from SMC5/6 loss to alveolar damage that does not pass through the immune defect. The cell type and intermediate steps are unknown; the founding authors speculated that loss of the NSMCE3-NSMCE4 interface specifically underlies the pulmonary phenotype.

nodes.description: The patient missense variants sit in the C-terminal winged-helix B domain (p.Pro209Leu) and its extension (p.Leu264Phe) of NSMCE3. nodes.description: The defining and fatal lesion. Lung biopsy and autopsy show diffuse alveolar damage with hyaline membranes, interstitial pneumonitis with lymphocyte-rich infiltrates, organizing pneumonia (including acute fibrinoid and organizing pneumonia), metaplastic squamous alveolar epithelium, lobular fibrosis and remodeling, and bronchiolitis obliterans, usually without evidence of active infection. Air leak (pneumomediastinum, pneumothorax, subcutaneous emphysema) complicates the course. Macrophage activation syndrome was not found. The authors attribute the failure of lung transplantation to the systemic nature of the disorder.
